provenance.construction: Halving of the two-block code [[64,18,8]] (codes/64-18-8.json) along the fixed-point-free ZX-duality that exchanges (1,h) and (2,c-h) (symplectic halving: Lee, Okada, Maskara, Kasai, Zhou, arXiv:2609.30069, Def. 3; Burton, Durso-Sabina, Brown, arXiv:2406.09951); equivalently the mirror code of Khesin and Lu (arXiv:2603.05496) with A = c - F_B, B = F_A. Parent: G = Z/2 x Z/4 x Z/4, element (a,b,e) with index 16a+4b+e; qubit (1,h) -> index of h, (2,h) -> 32 + index of h; X-check g on (1, g+F_A) and (2, g+F_B), Z-check g on (1, g-F_B) and (2, g-F_A), F_A = {(0,0,0),(0,0,3),(0,3,0),(1,3,3)}, F_B = {(0,0,0),(0,1,2),(0,3,3),(1,2,1)}; this is codes/64-18-8.json after renumbering G (the board file numbers G by GAP's Elements(SmallGroup(32,21))). Involution: Psi(1,h) = (2, c-h), Psi(2,h) = (1, c-h) with c = (1,1,0). Fold: fold qubit i is (1,h) with h of index i; the X-check g gives the generator with X on g+F_A and Z on c-g-F_B (Y where they meet), in the order of the X-checks. n = 32, rank 23, k = 9; 32 generators of weight 8, no Y factors; not locally Clifford equivalent to a CSS code.
provenance.notes: Distance 6 is exact: no nontrivial logical of Pauli weight <= 5 by three independent exhaustive computations (tropidist b03ec2d4077f in the board's Pauli encoding, certs/32-9-6.json in the same pull request; a meet-in-the-middle search of ours; Magma V2.30-1 MinimumDistance), and the witness has weight 6. Programs, data and logs: github.com/TimoKellerMath/quantum-error-correction @ 207d1130035a, folded-stabilizer-codes/. Not locally Clifford equivalent to a CSS code: the generator-level parity system for single-qubit Cliffords has no solution (an odd cycle closes at qubit 2 with generators 2 and 22), and every generator is the only nontrivial stabilizer supported in its support, so no single-qubit Clifford makes the group CSS. At board commit 8042f9da no stabilizer entry dominates or equals it; it dominates the stabilizer entries 36-7-6 (on n and k) and 40-9-6 (on n). It is a mirror code of Khesin and Lu (arXiv:2603.05496) on Z/2 x Z/4 x Z/4 with |A| = |B| = 4; their code table has no codes of check weight 8, and in the sources of our literature check (summarized in the README of folded-stabilizer-codes/) we found no published code with the parameters [[32,9,6]]. The tables of codetables.de list a [[32,9,7]] code, a dense code without weight restriction. No CSS entry dominates or equals it either. Checked, not equivalent to an existing entry.
